translations.text: Before the seed of quarrelsome mankind, the King who shines [?] before us went under a lofty, noble law: Christ, on the Kalends of January.
Isidore the bishop, abbot of a lofty church; Manchéne, splendour of the herd-places [?]; Scothíne, diadem of Mairge.
The great martyrdom of Rodanis [?] with his fair, wise clergy; Findlug with the excellence of nobility; Fintan, the sure one of Dún Bleisce.
The death in battle of Aquilinus with his troop, which was very strong; in the blood of Christ, through their bodies, they washed [?] their garments.
The calling of the venerable Simeon to Christ, a form that has shone [?]; he was a fair sun of a new champion, though [?] a hard, dark course.
Julian, a rock of purity, ran to the King of glorious choice; no outrage can touch the sound joy of the great baptism of Mary's Son.
The martyrdom of Lucian with a great host, it was most excellent; the beginning of Jesus' Lent has increased its nobility.
The death of Egemon [?], a devout, lofty bishop; Ercnat, descendant of Án, of the heritage [?]; Nechtan of noble form.
Fairest of hostages [?] in purity, before the King's face you have named [?]: godly, ardent Fáelán, fair Felix, Vitalis.
I beseech their splendid prayer, that no evil lot may befall me: Milit [?], holy, a fair helmet; Diarmait of Inis Clothrann.
The cross of the martyr Peter with a host full of valour; from Egypt, glorious the joy, came Mary's great Son.
The great martyrdom of Muscentius [?] with his fair, numerous clergy; Christ [?] ... [?] Laicenn, son of Báeth, the mighty [?].
May we have their blessing, a strong prayer without [?]: Sulpicius, eloquent and gentle; Hilary [?] (Clair), abbot of Poitiers.
The passion of Glycerius the deacon, who was loving to his Lord; the holy, renowned elder of Nola, Felix, ruddy, fair, blessed.
She helped, a wall against [?] great diseases; she loved great, heavy fasting: the bright sun of the women of Munster, Íte of Cluain Credail.
Devout ones [?] on the feast of Fursa, with whom they shared [?] the kingdom: nine thousand rich in victories, above twenty great thousands.
Let us praise them often, though [?] they are not [?] ...: the folk who suffered without guilt, on the feast of Anthony the monk.
The magnifying of Peter the apostle in Rome, a most excellent saying, along with the festival that is noblest, the great death of the mother of Jesus.
The death of Marius [?] and Martha with the yoke that binds them [?], along with the feast, with nobility, of fair old Paul, with Áine [?].
The splendid four, with virginity, on one festival, it is holiest: Molocca, Moecca, Sebastian, and Oenu.
May there be one condemnation [?] ... to the King, a course that is most excellent; Fainche [?] ...; noblest is Agnes, daughter of Jesus.
The death of the daughters of Comgall; Colmán son of Ua Beona; Valerius without disgrace; Felix, who found a melodious circuit.
The suffering of Severianus, of Clement, with [?] ... may they protect us to the King with [?] ... gifts [?].
For my soul, for my little body, may there be a wall against every weakness [?]: Babylas, a glow of bright gold, with his three little weaklings.
Not slight is the day of the festival on which cries are sent up to Christ, every [?] host [?]: of Paul, about [?] the judgment of baptism [?].
Mighty is their hosting with the King who has [?] them: a host slain after hunger, with the passion of Polycarp.
Máeda loved Muirgein, a wondrous birth with victories; Agnes won a pure victory before kings [?].
With the longing of John, the passion of eight virgins with Anna; they won victory with uprightness, the great host of Mesoranus.
The bishops [?] whom I have named, may they protect us for our forgiveness: Hippolytus, Paul, Gildas, Constantine.
A hundred and sixty martyrs, a great martyrdom [?]; [?] Énán of Ross Rind, the radiant.
Name Áed of Ferns the strong, Máel Anfaid, a name before us; with a very great King they win a fair crown over the host of January.
The Kalends of February magnify a shower of martyrs of great valour; Brigit, a strong, famous woman, chaste head of the nuns of Ireland.
The presentation of Mary's Son in the temple, sure and glorious; a great host of gentle martyrs with fair [?] of the fierce fist [?].
May Colán always help us [?] in his [?]; a fair hosting with the feast of Felix and Symphronius.
Fronius and Magnus, Gelasius the confessor, German a noble martyr, Crescens kindly and devout.
The shapely [?] body of Agatha, the champion, with purity, with Jesus with her pledge [?]; Tathus, great and good [?].
Andrew, high his dignity, a bishop [?], diadem of the kingdom; Lucia with Anna, whom thousands did not move.
Mellán of Inis Uasal, the son of Ua Cuinn who is not [?]; Lommán of Loch Brige [?], a high pillar of Loch Uair.
Ua Án of the Déisi, his speech was about Christ; Fiachra was a manly man, the wondrous abbot of Irard.
Mo-Chuaróc of wisdom, a saint who did not endure [?] baseness; Cairech Dergán the godly, Bishop Rónán the kingly.
A fair star, a birth of victory, a glow of gold, a bright pillar: Crónán the chaste, without baseness, the bright sun of Glas Mór.
Mo-Gopnat with pure [?], he was joyful in the love of Christ; it was good to him [?] always to call on Him [?], beloved Bishop Etchen.
Around Bishop Simplex a chief host, proven, was cut down; Damian, a soldier, diadem of martyrdom, with fair crucified companions.
In a little boat from the east over the [?] sea Modomnoc brought the mighty, famous seed of the bees [?] of Ireland.
On the battlefield of Valentine, Marcellus was tortured; in Christ's kingdom eighty [?] were planted.
Fair is the celebration of Sunday on the morrow after night [?]; with the passion of a mighty host, the victory of the Son of God [?].
Juliana [?], her name [?] to the border [?]; with [?] the tale of her [?], the demon [?].
Let everyone proclaim to the great sea the feast of Cormac with pure [?], with the feast of Fintan, the [?] of vast Clonenagh.
The chaste Colmán died; Mo-Lipa [?] him, on the feast of true men with holiness, Rutulus and Silvanus.
Name, with the passion of Publius, the passion of Marcellus, a victorious diadem, and of great, generous Baíthíne, the kindly son of Caindelda [?].
Gaius the bishop: his passion is not hidden. In a massacre (a sorrowful tale) twenty wise champions [died].
The calling of Fintan Corach after his contempt of the world, on the feast of the man of pure body [?], pleasant Virulus.
In Antioch was the ordination of Peter; wisdom declares it. The birth of Laurence, full of answers [?], together with the feast of shining Thecla.
Matthias the apostle suffered tortures for Christ. May he protect us to the kingdom, together with everyone he pledges for.
With the passion of Lucianus, the priest who crucified demons; the abbot of Iona, splendid in wisdom, excellent Cummíne the Fair.
The head of Paul the apostle was found, the devout champion [?], on the feast of the [?] man, strong Theolis, given to fasting.
The calling of Alexander into the dwelling of the saints. On one feast, with full fire [?], the birth of the Darcelli [?].
With the passion of Abundius, if you dare to sing great lays, tell of the feast of Congan the warrior, and the finding of the head of John.
On the feast of Sillán of Bangor, ten shapely holy virgins, together with the passion of a manly host, bring February to its end.
On the kalends of the month of March, magnify them against your evils [?]: Senán, Moínenn, Moses, David of Kilmuine (St Davids).
If feasts are commemorated: the passion of Lucilla, the birth of Paul the Elder (salvation be his), the feast of Fergna the Fair of Iona.
In the passion of Florianus [?], who has gone before us with eager zeal [?]; Christ's fair servant Erail; Mochrú son of Senán.
Tell of the passion of the bishop in royal, fair-lighted Rome, with a vast angelic host: Lucius, a radiant light.
His fame, no silent thing, has leapt over the eastern sea: royal Carthach of Rome [?]; Ciarán of Saigir with his hosts.
May they protect us, after devotion, to the kingdom of God on the straight way: the host of Orta [?] with Anianus [?], on the feast of Victorinus.
Beloved is the godly pair, who do not deserve unworthiness from our poem: holy Felicity, excellent Perpetua.
Senán of Inis Cathaig, who shook off shameful enemies, with a victorious assembly [?]; the warlike bishop Beóáed.
The death of forty soldiers, a great host that was most bright, for whom, against great cold [?], the sun rose in a black, dark place.
Fair, radiant Constantine was called to the angels; by him was found the angelic tree, the tree of the cross of the Lord.
They are companions of our Lord in the kingdom above kingdoms: Liberén, eternal Senán, Constantine king of Rathan.
Before reaching his land he crucified his body for Christ, the gathering [?] of a hundred virtues: Gregory of Rome, most eager.
May Mochoemóc protect us to the everlasting bliss that will be; holy Cuangus with prosperity [?]; of Liath Mór, a good pair.
Dionysius the bishop, whose companies are fair; may he who bears Christ's name, Salvator, protect us and set us free.
Set in order James of dignity, Lucas of beauty above tresses [?]; they loved secret converse with Christ: the sons of Nessan of the Island (Ireland's Eye).
Beloved, except to the demon, is Eugenia in the world; Abbán, an angelic bush of gold; radiant Finán the Leper.
The blaze of a splendid sun, the apostle of virgin Ireland, Patrick with a host of thousands: may he be a shelter for our wretchedness.
With a great troop of martyrs comes Nabor of many [?]; with [?] sixty mighty soldiers were counted.
Molachtóc, with Gregory of the most eminent champion rank [?]; Joseph, the noblest name, the beautiful foster-father of Jesus.
The death of Polychronius, a holy bishop, the most venerable; he took [?] the straightest step, with the great host of Badanus [?].
Donbith [?], of great victory; Benedict, a strong pillar; on the same feast, of the hosts of the sea [?], famous Enda of Aran.
The high passion of Secundus without [?] his words [?] ... strong [?] ... [?]; Failbe, splendid one [?] of Iona.
The [?] daughter of Dálach; Feradach, who is most lofty [?]; from Christ he declares [?] dignity, Mo-Medóc, the diadem of Scotland.
The [?] couple who strove [?] at abstinence [?]: Ainbech, fair Scire, beloved Tredan, Mochta, pious Credal.
The crucifixion and the conception of Jesus Christ [?] on the same feast, diligently, with the passion of James.
In [?] Mochellóc fell, after days [?]; the feast of the eternal [?] of Cell Aidbile [?] of Achad [?].
On the sixth of the Kalends of April, after the loosing of souls, Jesus arose—great tidings—from the womb of the earth.
May he who called us set us free; may he bless us past the pains; may Mary magnify us, the great Magdalene.
With the feast of the daughters of Baíth, the death of a great host with modesty [?]; on the feast of a man of true virginity, Gregory of Nazareth [?].
Name Mochua of Balla, a [?] with dignity; Ainbech [?]; Colmán of Linn [?]; with the feast of pious Tola.
The cross of splendid Ninach [?], with a fair clergy most beautiful [?]; Martha gives a crown for ever upon the swarming host [?].
Ambrose, with greatness of purity, ennobles the Kalends of April; the greatest joy is held by a feast among the feasts of Mary.
The great host of Amphianus, to whom the world was gloomy, sprang [?], after a hard battle, into the noble, joyful peace.
The host of noble Evagrius, who cast off [?] ... [?] with treasures [?]; forty [?] high, fair hundreds.
Fair is pious Tigernach, for Christ [?] every death [?], from whom bursts a stream of wisdom [?], of Clúain Eois [?].
On the great feast of Mac Cuilinn [?], Beccán with the victory of diligence; the baptism [?] of chief Patrick was [?] in Ireland.
Herenius the bishop, great are his thousands; a fair bush with virginity before the Lord of the fair host [?].
Fínán Cam of Cenn Etig, around whom [?] great [?]; Christ's fair champion [?], from Slíab Bladma, Bledma [?].
The death of Enair [?] the martyr, he was a great pillar of the temple; not refused [?] before his community was the head of Faílad, abbot of Bangor.
The victory of the seven holy virgins of [?] in every dwelling [?] ... from their blood that is not quenched [?], with the fair feast of Quadratus.
The cross of Apollonius the priest, for Christ [?] they endured [?]; from Ross Eó, a joyful name, [?] royal [?].
May Máedóc the treasure-rich protect us; he is a warlike brother. A descendant of Dúnlang, though he was made holy; certain, [?] (dálach).
The love [?] of Christ's work set him apart [?] for the bounds of a relic [?]: Julius, bishop, abbot of the people, the noble prop of Peter's seat.
With his happy chief host, who [?] against every mouth, [?] (geraitcristcain) went Paul the deacon; may he redeem us [?].
The royal bishop Tassach, when he came to him, gave the body of Christ, the truly strong King, with communion to Patrick.
A pre-eminent flame that does not die down, against the onslaught of wilful desire; a fair precious stone was Ruadán, lamp of Lorrha.
With royal Carissa out of Rome's burial-place, the feast of the deacon Felix comes to you [?] (forsidit).
On the feast of Peter the deacon, who sprang [?] to a martyrdom of victory, with his fair company of clergy went Donnán of cold Eigg.
On the feast of Septimus, the noble deacon, Laisrén, a victorious flame, beautiful abbot of Leighlin, is present [?] to console [?].
Famous Hermogenes went, after finishing his fight, to Jesus: a splendid turning out of his cold little body of clay.
With the passion of Heraclius [?], a crucified priest [?] (tuile); a feast in Rome, glorious place, of the saints of all Europe.
Into Scotland in purity, after leaving every pleasure, went from us with his mother our brother Máel Rubai.
May Philip the apostle protect us, who is greater than every fast; whose name, by the mystery [?] of the Father, is 'Mouth of a broad lamp'.
The lightning-flash, Bishop Ibar, who struck down the head of every heresy, a splendid flame over the wave [?] (trilis), died in Little Ireland (Beggery).
The victory of the three pure youths in the furnace, a famous company; the passion of George, sun of victory, with thirty great thousands.
Noble Mark in Egypt, who allowed no word of neglect; a rod of gold, a mighty bar [?], the great bishop Mac Caille.
Fair Cyril, a captive, suffered a field of spear-points for Christ, every splendid one [?], with a vast host around him.
Angels used to bring [?] him out of prisons, though he used to go [?] into them: noble Alexander, abbot of Rome of the faith [?].
Christopher, with Crónán of Roscrea, steadfastly on his feast without pride; a great company [?] of soldiers went to martyrdom.
The martyrdom of Germanus, Christ's priest, great was his coming [?]; with the fair daughter of Uaithne on one feast with Fiachra.
They close April's clergy, for it is clearly that he counts them: Rónán of Lethros [?] (huamni), in Rome the cross of Quirinus.
The Kalends of [?] (nethchoimi) May: the birth of Philip, most eminent [?]; there began, most noble, the lovely preaching of Jesus.
The departure of Saturninus to Christ came about, with the death, after long sighing, of Nechtan, Patrick's fosterling.
The first finding of the wood of Christ's cross with a multitude of virtues; the death of Conláed, a fair pillar; the great feast of Mary the Virgin [?].
On the passion of Anterus [?], fair Mochua went, son of renowned Cuinnen, on the feast of Silvanus the deacon.
The deacon Eutimius with Hilary went beyond pains on a feast-day which our Lord raised up [?].
The man who first wrote the fair tales of crucified Christ, he is honoured together with his kingdom [?]: the great birth (feast) of glorious Matthew.
Mo-Chiaróc with Breccán, the two most [?] and purest; they loved Christ, who is dearest, in Echdruim of the oaks.
Victor and Maximus came together around Christ; for love of the King whom they loved, they bathed in their blood.
A great manifestation of Michael to the world, a proven story; the passion of Cyril, fair and beloved; Bishop Santan, renowned.
Peace-prince of the altar, around which is the sound of every church: may he protect us, the host-leading, victorious Comgall of Bangor.
The victory of Job, who did not forget the King of the clouds, was very bright [?]; Mo-Chritóc, fair household, and the priest Cormac.
Cyriacus, crucified by thirties [?], betroths [?] pilgrims; a precious name, with holy Erc, binding [?].
The holy household of Tarachus and Probus, after journeys [?], after long, bitter crucifixions: six persons and six hundred.
Corona and Victor with his clergy, without [?], in one festival, an everlasting sea [?]; the fair feast of Carthach of Rahan.
The sevenfold grace of the Spirit came down on a bright-white clergy; solemn Sárán; the rich feast of great Dublitir.
The calling of Brendan of Clonfert into the victorious eternal kingdom; the holy death of Cairnech, truly strong, together with the noble feast of Ua Suanaig.
The host of Adrion [?], of Victor, of Basilla, they were set loose [?] without portion [?]; [?] over the [?] of the realm of Finne [?].
The feast of Mark, well was he crowned; my great Medóc, rich in treasures; Modomnóc, a victorious diadem; the feast of Bran Becc of Clane.
The clergy of Urban, pure, in whom no lusts were born; their souls are white through the shedding of their blood.
The great blood of Marcellus [?] went under the earth [?] [?]; in one festival Gervasius and Protasius are invoked.
Solemn martyr, a great wonder [?], [?] of the two of Turin [?]; Colmán the leper, [?]; Barrind of Druim Cuilinn.
The soul of Ronán Find stepped to starry heaven, along with the fair man of many children [?], Baíthéne son of Finnach.
The bright host of Epictetus, which is bold, which is steadfast; after suffering under torment, it was welcomed by angels.
Augustine the bishop; Hermes, great abbot of a thousand; Colmán, a beloved pillar of greatness [?]; Tuathach of the land [?].
[?] the feast of John, beloved pillar of virginity; Dionysius, sure and bold; Dunchad of Iona, noble.
[?] the choir of Colmán; name Stella [?] without [?]; Beccán loved vigils [?] in Cluain Aird, his dwelling.
Acolius the priest with his clergy, which is holiest; their blood, before every generation [?], was shed together.
May they protect us with the angels, a beloved, happy throng [?]: Germanus, sun of the elders, foster-father of Patrick of Armagh.
The great host of Pollio, may they protect us [?]; with Cummain of pure fame, the beloved daughter of Allen.
The holy apostle [?] in the foundations of wisdom; the birth (feast) of Thomas without [?], in the foundations of wisdom.
The passion of Chrysogonus, with the passion of Paternella [?]; a greater month [?], as great as a thousand, of chief feasts [?].
A treasure of the mind is the feast of Thecla, a high and splendid protection [?], [?] with a vast and noble host, at the front of the kalends of June.
Erasmus the bishop, a fiery blaze with the fervour of might, brought to Christ a victorious company, thirty praiseworthy thousands.
A soldier of Christ in the land of Ireland, a high name over the wave, [?]; Kevin (Cóemgen), chaste and fair, a champion [?] of the broad Glen of the Two Lakes (Glendalough).
Apollinaris went straight to the kingdom of God with his clergy, wholly, along with the translation of Martin.
The martyrdom of Marcianus, [?] of many victories; the praise [?] of Fer Mór of good kindred; the praise [?] of a virgin maiden.
The complete passion of Amantius, a great deed which he endured [?]; Máel Aithchen with pure lips went under the earth's covering.
The calling of Paul the martyr after a great deed, with strength; the feast of Colum, without arrogance, the great son of Ua Artai.
The reception of holy Job after victory and white martyrdom [?]; the feast of Medrán, a great consolation; the feast of Murchú, with great grace.
May they protect us into the everlasting kingdom, about which is a living, radiant enclosure: Baithéne, lofty and angelic, and Colum Cille, the shining lamp.
They meet on one path—happy is he who has come upon them [?]—the chief feast of Mark, a famous diadem, with the victorious feast of Barnabas.
Basilla the victorious was borne away from us in joy; the feast of the holy son of Tál, with the passion of Fortunatus.
The feast of the devout Cóemán, whose surname is Santlethan; [?] lasting, [?], over the broad sea full of ships.
With eminent Bartholomew—feeble are those who have not heard [?] every [?] from us to [?]—chaste Mac Nisse of Cluain.
They meet, both together, on one festival, devoted and attended by hosts: Nem son of Ua Birn the mighty, with victorious Benedict.
A blessing on the champion who loved Christ with true [?], with whom a host went with great valour: Vitus, the child of miracles.
My champion is Quiricus [?], to whom a joyful host bowed down; neither path nor likeness to him was found among the sons of the world.
The golden bush from the borders, the splendid sun above the peoples, with the zeal [?] of a strong king's brother: the fair soldier Moling Lúachair.
With Báethán, fair and blessed, [?] keenly [?], the sons of Moenán, wholly, from stony Land Léire.
Their blood went forth together before hosts, boldly, to the King; they were worthy: Gervasius and Protasius.
The passion of Paul and of Cyriacus, with that great host; Fáelán with that victory, that splendid dumb one.
A famous champion, attended by hosts, against whom the sea burst forth [?]: Cormac [?], the cleric, the beautiful [?] Ua Liatháin.
With James son of Alphaeus came a bright company of a hundred; the feast of a man who did not love bodily [?]: Crónán the mighty [?], Ferán [?].
The commemoration of Mochoe—there is none [?]; the famous, blessed pillar from Nendrum [?].
The royal birth of John the Baptist—if you have diligently attended to it—with the translation, without reproach, of John the son [?] to Ephesus.
The feast of Sinchell, the feast of Telle: they were a tree whose hand-price was high [?]; a pure-bright sun, a splendour of great form.
Vast was their suffering, the passion that pierced [?] them: the fair sun Gallicanus, John and Paul.
Proven were their martyrdoms, great their heavy sufferings: seven true brothers of the city, in Rome of broad, wide Latium.
Illecoin [?] the great of Meath, Cruimmíne with Conán, on one feast-day; clearly shines the fair passion of Fabian.
The feast of Paul and Peter, with the vastness of their ardour [?]; the din of battle did not overcome them; a feast that is on the bosoms of the world.
The victory of Sole [?] is splendid; the death of beloved Job; they strike [?] a fair green ... [?] upon the host [?] of June of many treasures.
On the kalends of July, the great wonders which Matthew [?] ...; the bitter death of Aaron; the elders Simon and Thaddeus.
The death of Eutychius [?], bishop of Damascus, with splendour; the kingly passion of Processus; the great torment of Martinian.
The martyrdom of Cirion of Christ [?] ... [?]; ... [?] a feast ... [?].
The great good honour of Martin ... [?], with a hundred wondrous martyrs; Finnbarr of Inis Doimle.
The martyr Agatho with his clergy, a fair company; Christ granted [?] smooth peace; his great love with Laomun [?].
Moninne of Slieve Cuilinn, she was a fair pillar; she won the victory of bright purity, sister of great Mary.
With his great host, splendid Parmenius, a mighty company [?]; Máel Ruain reached heaven, the noble sun of the island of the Gaels.
Brocán the scribe won noble victory [?] ... [?], with Diarmait, sure; Lassar, the bright sun of Glenn Uissen.
Declare the name of Onchú, Mo-Stic; everyone who entreats him [?] ...; they loved Christ: Lére, Garbán of Kinsale [?].
Declare the passion of the seven brothers, whose cross was the cross of Christ; ... [?]; great Mark, Sostan [?]; two thousand martyrs.
With the martyrdom of the queen Euphemia of the hosts; strong Benedict, a pillar; the devout son Conlocha [?].
Nazarius went to the angels, a tale for every synod; Felix, good was his tomb [?], with his great host ... [?].
Sweet is the name, with splendour, of holy Evangelius; with Siloc [?] of the royal company he went into noble peace [?].
May Bishop James protect us, he is the holiest; we will beseech [?] ... [?] with ten [?] infants [?].
The twelve apostles who teach [?] every region; Jesus of the seed of Adam distributed them before the countless host.
Every day there will come to Christ — provided they agree in prayer [?] — with his host the gentle little boy Mammes [?].
May the prayers horum atque harum ('of these men and of these women') magnify us, of every martyr we number, along with the host of the Scillitans.
May the hosting of the queens protect us in noble peace, with a great band of seven brothers, in holy Christina [?].
The holy prayer of Sisinnius ... [?]; may it come [?] ... to help [?], with the great company of Brestae [?].
Spirited are the maidens: noble, unblemished Sabina; Romula the Roman, with pious Quirinus [?].
The lofty cross of Elias the martyr; they magnify [?] the entombed relics, with a comely band of maidens; the passion of prosperous Praxedis.
Fair-born Mary Magdalene, the diadem of every host; the passion of noble Apollinaris; Mobíu of Inis Cuscraid.
With the passion of Vincent a host went to Christ in Rome; it was a venerable course: twice nine good soldiers.
If you want help, O Ireland, a champion in battle, you have the head of a hundred thousand: Declan of Ardmore.
Mo-Cholmóc, Mo-Shílóc, with Nessán on their Lammas [?]; James, a champion: tell of the death of the brother of John.
At the passion of Jovian with his fair clergy of pure gold; the Transfiguration of Jesus on Mount Tabor after evening twilight [?].
The death of Simeon the monk, who was a great sun to the earth; with the passion of a beloved host in high, vast Antioch.
Vast is their help, with their shining hosting: Theophilus, an angelic tower of gold; radiant Pantaleon.
Lupus and Simplicius, bishops without any share of shame; Prosper with a complete clergy, the kingly stars.
They used to sing Christ's law and searched it out with its mysteries; with a host in whom no wrongdoing was found, Abdon and Sennen.
May the host of July, with its ... [?] thousands, protect you, lofty pillar; a glorious bishop of Ireland, Colmán son of Dáráne.
On the Kalends of August great might has arrived, with the feast of the Maccabee sons, eighty great thousands.
With the mother who survived [?], Theodota, at that time; those three good little sons went to that victory.
The metropolitan ... [?] willingly, with certain rejoicing [?], with Ani [?] in the assembly, with the holiness of the little body of noble Stephen.
He will be joyful after coming to me [?]; great is his ... [?]: the kingly, gentle champion, Molua son of Oche.
The glorious passion of Herentius [?], a lofty, fair protection; with holy Oswald of ... [?], noble high king of the Saxons.
Sixtus, bishop of the Romans, bore a swimming swarm [?] up to heaven; Lommchú, a victorious pillar, from Clondalkin of the assemblies.
Proclaim five above three fifties of years, a mighty matter, that seven without reproach watched over us [?], who slept in unknowing.
The feast of Beóán son of Nessán, great [?], not a feeble request [?]; Colmán, a bishop of beauty, from Inishbofin.
Keep with you [?] the passion of Antoninus, of Firmus, a strong household; in fair Achad Claintair, Nathí, a devout priest.
The full cross of Laurence the deacon, whose little body was hardy, with a whole, noble, ... [?] host; fair Bláán of Kingarth.
Pray to wise Airennán, whose fame is not concealed, with pure Valerian and strong, prudent Tiburtius.
The summoning of Laisrén of great Inis Muiredaig; Mochta with a great clergy; may the feast of famous Ségéne never fade.
Hippolytus the martyr, his ... [?] was a wonder, with a vast, noble host; Mo-Medóc, diadem of the Gaels.
